entities.name: Cristina, daughter of Edward the Exile
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cristina, a princess of the venerable House of Wessex, was the daughter of Edward the Exile and sister to Edgar Ætheling and Saint Margaret of Scotland, born in Hungary around 1040-1045. As a direct descendant of King Edmund Ironside, her life spanned the tumultuous period of the Norman Conquest, making her a crucial link between the deposed Anglo-Saxon monarchy and the new Norman dynasty. Her decision to become a nun at Romsey Abbey after 1070 provided a sanctuary for her royal lineage and positioned her to influence the next generation of Anglo-Scottish royalty, notably through her guardianship of her nieces, Matilda and Mary of Scotland.

Born during her family's long exile in Hungary, Cristina returned to England in 1057 with her father, who had been recalled by Edward the Confessor as a potential heir to the English throne. Following the death of Edward the Confessor in January 1066 and the subsequent Norman Conquest later that year, Cristina, her mother Agatha, and her siblings fled north, eventually seeking refuge in Scotland. By 1070, she had taken vows as a nun at Romsey Abbey in Hampshire, a move that offered both personal devotion and a degree of political neutrality for a member of the Anglo-Saxon royal line. Within the abbey, she assumed the significant role of educating and protecting her nieces, Matilda and Mary, the daughters of her sister Margaret and King Malcolm III of Scotland.
